title: What is Vector OS?
description: Understand the Vector OS engineering workspace, Design and Project layouts, beta connector availability and the difference between website samples and native work.
html:
Home/Product

The engineering workspace

What is Vector OS?

Vector OS is an engineering workspace for planning, building and reviewing work with your existing tools. This website offers interactive samples and recorded examples. Work in an engineering application requires the installed Vector OS app, an available connector and a supported build.

Understand. Plan. Review the result.

Ask
Understand the context you select before proposing a change.
Plan
Review the intended steps, affected objects and expected result.
Build
A native change requires approval and a fresh check of the selected host and document. Follow the exact build’s requirements.

These task modes describe the kind of request. They are separate from the workspace layout. The guides explain selected context, approval and recovery checkpoints. Read the task-mode guide or check native approval.

Choose your workspace view.

Design provides a focused agent view. Project adds the project and conversation sidebar around the sample. In the website preview, switching layouts keeps your selected sample project, draft and host during that session.

Compare Design and Project

Which tools are available?

The following tools are labelled Available in the Vector OS beta. Supported features, modules and host versions depend on your build.

  • Rhino
  • Revit
  • Blender
  • Maxsurf Complete

In development Grasshopper and Dynamo. Their availability is separate from the paired Rhino and Revit entries. Upcoming tools are discovery entries; a listing does not announce connector development or a release date.

Browse all software and connector statuses

How does AI connect to CAD?

A software connector links an installed engineering application to the workspace. Start with its current availability, a compatible build and a specific task. Read the AI connection guide or explore AI workflows by software.

How can I try it?

Request Windows beta access and the requirements for your tools. A qualified public installer is not currently offered on the download page. Access and compatibility are checked separately; browsing an example does not confirm either. Read the installation guide.

Use the interactive preview to explore the interface, or watch recorded projects. Website samples use scripted data and do not connect to or change your CAD software. See recorded examples or learn about selected context.
